answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may transact. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, and any identity caught misbehaving loses its deposit, so the attack's price grows linearly while its payoff stays flat. New identities also start at the nadir of trust and must earn standing through verified work, like a garden that only yields after seasons of tending: one honest agent's plume of reputation is cheap to grow once, but a Sybil farmer must tend thousands of gardens at once, which no budget survives.
